value.overview: The White-throated Mountain-gem is a small hummingbird of Central American highlands. It is associated mainly with humid montane forests, especially oak woodland, forest edges, and shrubby clearings. Males have a white throat and bright green upperparts, while females are more subdued and have rufous underparts. The species is resident rather than a long-distance migrant. Taxonomic treatments vary, and some populations in southern Costa Rica have been treated as the Gray-tailed Mountain-gem, Lampornis cinereicauda.
value.classification: The White-throated Mountain-gem belongs to the hummingbird family Trochilidae and the genus Lampornis. It is sometimes included in a broader mountain-gem species complex because of close similarities with related forms.
value.identification: This hummingbird is about 12 cm long and has a straight, medium-length black bill. Adult males show dark bronzy-green upperparts, an emerald-green crown, a white chin and throat, bright green sides of the neck and upper breast, and a dark gray lower breast and belly. Females have green upperparts, a darker rufous throat and belly, and paler outer tail feathers. The white throat and highland habitat help distinguish the male from other mountain-gems.
value.rangeHabitat: The White-throated Mountain-gem occurs in the highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama. In Costa Rica, it is reported as a resident of montane oak forests, especially in the Cordillera de Talamanca and adjacent south-central highlands, extending southward toward Panama. It uses forest interiors, edges, secondary growth, shrubby clearings, and sometimes gardens near woodland. Records and taxonomic treatments differ in southern Costa Rica, where some birds have been assigned to the Gray-tailed Mountain-gem. It generally occupies elevations from about 1,500 m to timberline.
value.migrationStatus: It is generally considered a year-round resident in Costa Rica and elsewhere in its range. Local movements may occur with flowering conditions or elevation, but regular long-distance migration is not known.
value.breeding: Breeding has been reported mainly from October through April. The female builds a small cup-shaped nest from fine plant fibers, with moss and sometimes lichen attached to the outside. Nests are placed in vegetation in montane forest or nearby shrubby habitat. Available information on clutch details, incubation duration, and nestling development is limited, and the male is not known to provide parental care.
value.dietFeeding: The species feeds mainly on nectar from a variety of flowering plants and is an important pollinator of highland vegetation. Males often defend flower patches in the forest interior, while females may forage more frequently in shrubby areas and along edges. It also captures or gleans small arthropods from foliage, which provide essential protein, especially during breeding and when feeding young.
value.behavior: White-throated Mountain-gems are active during daylight and usually forage alone. Males are territorial and can dominate smaller hummingbirds at rich flower sources, although larger hummingbirds may displace them. The species commonly moves rapidly between flowers, perches in shaded vegetation, and gives sharp, high-pitched calls. Its preference for forest edges and clearings allows it to use both relatively undisturbed woodland and suitable human-modified highland habitats.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population size and population trend are not well quantified.
